# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixteen at death  <sub>[v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v3 c14 P37](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0037)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c26 P58](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0058), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal was a striking young woman with radiant skin, bright blue eyes, and long, lovely yellow hair that she wore in braids or styled up. She had a full, eye-catching figure and was regarded as the most beautiful girl at Regent's Academy. During her illness, she grew extremely slender, with see-through hands and a feverish flush on her cheeks.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)_

## Personality

Opal possessed a sunny, cheerful, and merry disposition, though she was heavily inclined toward sentimentality and obsessed with romantic attention and suitors. She delighted in social gatherings, laughter, teasing her admirers, and boasting about her beaus. Beneath her superficial vanity, she possessed a deep love for children, a terror of death, and a genuine attachment to her childhood friends.

_Sources: [v1 c26 P6](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0006), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c11 P58](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0058), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P37](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0037)_

## History

Opal attended Brierley school, where she shared desks and games with Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen. She joined the school's Story Club, participated in recitations and concerts, and played games along the pond. She later progressed to the Regent's class and attended Regent's Academy in Port Marlow. After completing her studies, she secured a position teaching at the Delford school. During her adolescence, Opal was constantly surrounded by suitors, rejecting Nelson Atkins after realizing he copied his proposal from an etiquette book. She later contracted a severe chest congestion during the winter, which developed into galloping consumption. Forced to stop teaching, she harbored hopes of resuming her career at Pale Sands school. As her condition deteriorated throughout the summer, she shared an emotional conversation in her garden with Nell Harcourt, confessing her terror of dying young. Shortly after, Opal passed away peacefully in her sleep and was buried in the Brierley cemetery.

## Background by volume

- Belongs to the Pettigrew family of Brierley and has numerous older sisters  <sub>[v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c26 P17](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0017)</sub>
- Her sister Tabitha married Malcolm Andres  <sub>[v1 c26 P17](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0017)</sub>
- Cured her warts using an enchanted stone from old Mary Joe  <sub>[v1 c16 P18](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0018)</sub>

## Quotes

> Floating downward does not bother me when two or three of us are occupying the flat and we are able to sit upright. During those times, it is enjoyable. However, lying flat and acting as if I were deceased—that is something I simply could not do. Fear would actually kill me.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Will you come up frequently, Nell? Make sure to come by yourself—I need you.  <sub>[v3 c11 P55](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0055)</sub>

> Nell, the time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)</sub>

> And, oh, Nell—dying is not what I want. The thought of dying frightens me.  <sub>[v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live the way other girls do. I—I desire to get married, Nell—and—and—possess tiny children. You are aware that babies were always something I loved, Nell.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
